title: How prefixes change what a word means
examples: Why does misspell have two s letters?

explain.say: Think of the word happy, the way you feel on your birthday. Look at the board: happy is the root word, the main part of the word. Now watch what happens when I stick something on the front.

draw.text: How prefixes change what a word means

explain.say: See the front chunk light up? un. A small chunk added at the start of a word is called a prefix. un means not, so unhappy means not happy. Can you make the word that means not kind?
Here is another prefix on the board: re. It means again. So rewrite means write again, and replay means play again. What do you think refill means?
Look at dis on the board. It flips a word into its opposite: agree becomes disagree, and appear becomes disappear. Notice the root word never changes its spelling. We just add the prefix in front.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: dis turns a word into its opposite

explain.say: You are a word builder now! The board sorts prefixes by what they mean. Look at the before group: a preview comes before the film. Wow: prehistoric means from before history was written down!

faq.a: A prefix is a group of letters added to the front of a word to change its meaning, like un in unhappy or re in redo.

faq.q: Does a prefix change the spelling of the root word?
faq.a: No. You just put the prefix in front. That is why misspell has two s letters and unnecessary has two n letters: mis plus spell, un plus necessary.
asks: Why does misspell have two s letters?

faq.a: un means not. Unhappy means not happy, unfair means not fair and unsafe means not safe.
pre means before. Preheat the oven means heat it before cooking, and a preview is a look before the real thing.
Many come from Latin and Greek: re, pre and dis from Latin, and anti and tele from Greek. Tele means far, so a telephone carries sound far.

facts: A study of school books found that four prefixes, un, re, in and dis, make up more than half of all words with prefixes.
Tele comes from Greek for far: telephone, television and telescope all share it.

quiz.why: re means again, so reheat means heat again.

wrong.0: Not would be the prefix un.

quiz.why: Add the prefix mis to spell without changing either part.

wrong.1: mis plus spell keeps both s letters.
